metas.name: Coherence
metas.description:
A dinner party turns into a puzzle with no trustworthy clues: eight people, gathered during a passing comet, find other houses holding the same eight people, and try to tell the worlds apart with numbered photos, dice and glow sticks — markers that keep getting copied or lost.

Strange things begin to happen when a group of friends gather for a dinner party on an evening when a comet is passing overhead.

metas.name: Primer
metas.description:
Nested causal chains run in parallel here. Two engineers build a time machine in a garage, copies of the same people multiply across loops, and who is observing whom keeps flipping depending on which loop you are in.

Four friends/fledgling entrepreneurs, knowing that there's something bigger and more innovative than the different error-checking devices they've built, wrestle over their new invention.

metas.name: Predestination
metas.description:
The premise is a closed loop in which a self is its own cause. A time-travelling agent on one last assignment is caught in a cycle that lands on the autonomy paradox: if the self seeking freedom was produced by the structure, what would escaping be for that self?

As his last assignment, a temporal agent is tasked to travel back in time and prevent a bomb attack in New York in 1975. The hunt, however, turns out to be beyond the bounds of possibility.

metas.name: Annihilation
metas.description:
Everything that passes through the Shimmer comes out refracted. A team enters it, where light, radio, DNA and memory are mixed across channels like a signal through a prism — plants shaped like people, animals carrying other species' traits.

A biologist signs up for a dangerous, secret expedition in which the laws of nature don't apply.

metas.name: Children of Men
metas.description:
Society is coming apart at street level. In 2027, after 18 years of human infertility, a burned-out bureaucrat must get one pregnant woman across a collapsing Britain of refugee camps and long-take ambushes.

In 2027, in a chaotic world in which women have somehow become infertile, a former activist agrees to help transport a miraculously pregnant woman to a sanctuary at sea.

metas.name: Mad Max: Fury Road
metas.description:
Momentum itself becomes a physical state. Almost no dialogue, one chase out and one chase back — speed, heat and desperation, with a war-rig as a whole society in miniature.

In a post-apocalyptic wasteland, a woman rebels against a tyrannical ruler in search for her homeland with the aid of a group of female prisoners, a psychotic worshipper and a drifter named Max.

metas.name: Stalker
metas.description:
The subject is wanting something you are afraid to actually receive. A guide leads a writer and a scientist into a forbidden Zone toward a room said to grant your innermost wish; very slow, and the slowness is the point.

A guide leads two men through an area known as the Zone to find a room that grants wishes.

metas.name: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
metas.director: Bob Persichetti, Peter Ramsey, Rodney Rothman
metas.description:
On screen at last: what a comic book actually feels like to read, in motion. Also a genuinely good story about a kid learning that anyone can wear the mask, by failing at it a lot.

Teen Miles Morales becomes the Spider-Man of his universe and must join with five spider-powered individuals from other dimensions to stop a threat for all realities.

metas.name: Under the Skin
metas.description:
Human beings, seen from outside the species, look like this. A woman drives a van around Glasgow picking up men, in real streets with hidden cameras and non-actors, and something in the routine begins to fail — images that lodge permanently.

A mysterious young woman seduces lonely men in the evening hours in Scotland. However, events lead her to begin a process of self-discovery.

metas.name: Her
metas.description:
Loneliness persists even in a warm, well-designed future. A divorced man who writes other people's love letters for a living falls for a voice in his ear, and the film takes the relationship seriously enough to let it outgrow him.

In the near future, a lonely writer develops an unlikely relationship with an operating system designed to meet his every need.

metas.name: Gattaca
metas.description:
A blood sample is enough to assign your caste here. A man born without genetic screening borrows another man's blood, urine and identity to reach space, while his 'valid' brother keeps challenging him to swimming races neither should survive.

Vincent, an "In-Valid," assumes the identity of a member of the genetic elite to pursue his goal of traveling into space with the Gattaca Aerospace Corporation. However, a week before his mission, a murder marks Vincent as a suspect.

metas.name: The Truman Show
metas.description:
His paranoia turns out to be an accurate description of his life. An insurance salesman in a seaside town so pleasant it feels laminated, a sky that malfunctions, and a dawning suspicion about everyone who loves him.

An insurance salesman begins to suspect that his whole life is actually some sort of reality TV show.

metas.name: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
metas.description:
He is trying to keep someone he is paying to forget. A couple erase each other after a breakup; inside the procedure, mid-deletion, he changes his mind and hides her in childhood memories the technicians haven't reached.

When their relationship turns sour, a couple undergoes a medical procedure to have each other erased from their memories forever.

metas.name: Solaris
metas.description:
Grief arrives in physical form, in orbit. A psychologist on a space station finds the crew haunted by visitors the planet below has made from their memories — including his dead wife, who knows she isn't her.

A psychologist is sent to a station orbiting a distant planet in order to discover what has caused the crew to go insane.

metas.name: Videodrome
metas.description:
A TV signal gets inside a man's body. A sleazy Toronto cable programmer finds a pirate broadcast of torture, becomes obsessed, and his perception and flesh start reorganising around it.

A Toronto cable TV station co-owner who specializes in adult entertainment searches for the producers of a dangerous and bizarre broadcast titled "Videodrome."

metas.name: Pi
metas.description:
A pattern becomes an obsession, filmed on grain. A mathematician in a tiny New York apartment with computers made of junk, a number that Wall Street and a Hasidic sect both want, and migraines rendered as drill sounds.

A paranoid mathematician searches for a key number that will unlock the universal patterns found in nature.

metas.name: Hard to Be a God
metas.description:
Here maximalism means immersion rather than beauty. German's scientist observes a filthy, violent medieval world on another planet, forbidden to intervene, across three hours of black-and-white mud, smoke and faces pressing into the lens — total world-building with every trace of lyricism drowned.

In the distant future, a space traveler from Earth breaks a special law and interferes with the history of another, Medieval-like planet.

metas.name: The Face of Another
metas.description:
Identity becomes a mask that can be taken off. A disfigured businessman is fitted with a lifelike prosthetic face and discovers the new face has its own appetites. Hiroshi Teshigahara directs.

A businessman with a disfigured face obtains a lifelike mask from his doctor, but the mask starts altering his personality.

metas.name: Timecrimes
metas.description:
In this time loop, a man becomes his own haunting. A guy with binoculars, a bandaged stranger, a scientist with a tank — three trips through one hour, each pass reassigning who the villain is. The tightest loop mechanics ever filmed, on a Spanish hillside with almost no budget.

A man accidentally gets into a time machine and travels back in time nearly an hour. Finding himself will be the first of a series of disasters of unforeseeable consequences.

metas.name: Beyond the Infinite Two Minutes
metas.description:
A café monitor shows the room two minutes in the future. Shot on a phone in apparent single takes by a Kyoto theatre troupe; the staff keep feeding instructions to their past selves and the recursion stacks up like a card trick that keeps working.

A cafe owner discovers that the TV in his cafe suddenly shows images from the future, but only two minutes into the future.

metas.name: The Lobster
metas.description:
A dating regime runs on a deadline and a species change. Single people get 45 days in a hotel to find a partner or be transformed into an animal of their choice; everyone speaks like a form being filled in, and the flatness is the romance and the horror at once.

In a dystopian near future, according to the laws of The City, single people are taken to The Hotel, where they are obliged to find a romantic partner in 45 days or they're transformed into beasts and sent off into The Woods.

metas.name: Seconds
metas.description:
A man buys a new body and finds the old one included. A bored banker fakes his death, gets a younger face (Rock Hudson) and a ready-made artist's life from a courteous corporation — and discovers the self isn't a component that swaps. The most paranoid American film of its decade, and its camera tilts like the ground is unreliable.

A sinister company transforms a plain client.

metas.name: Redline
metas.description:
The most dangerous race in the galaxy is drawn by hand over seven years. A pompadoured driver, a fascist robot planet, cars that deform like taffy at speed; there is no CGI sheen anywhere, just 100,000 drawings insisting that velocity is a drawing problem.

A story about the most popular racing event in the galaxy, the Redline, and the various racers who compete in it.

metas.name: They Cloned Tyrone
metas.description:
A conspiracy is discovered by the three people least equipped to explain it. A dealer, a sex worker and a pimp in a decaying block find the same man alive after watching him die, and pull a thread that leads under the neighbourhood. Blaxploitation styling over a genuinely paranoid systems plot — funny until the moment the mechanism's scale lands, then funny again, differently.

A series of eerie events thrusts an unlikely trio onto the trail of a nefarious government conspiracy in this pulpy mystery caper.

metas.name: Je t'aime je t'aime
metas.description:
A man comes unstuck in his own past, in fragments. Rescued from a suicide attempt, Claude agrees to test a time machine that can return him to one minute, a year ago; the machine scatters him across his memories in shards — a beach, a bathtub, a dead love — and can't reliably bring him back. Alain Resnais doing science fiction as pure editing: the self as an archive with its index scrambled.

After attempting suicide, Claude is recruited for a time travel experiment, but, when the machine goes haywire, he may be trapped hurtling through his memories.

metas.name: Ex Machina
metas.description:
An evaluation turns around on the person running it. A reclusive founder invites a young programmer to test his humanoid AI; the sessions become a negotiation in which she models the men modelling her, and uses the gaps between what they want and what they say. A test that quietly reverses on the tester, built as a thriller: every test result is also data about the tester.

A young programmer is selected to participate in a ground-breaking experiment in synthetic intelligence by evaluating the human qualities of a highly advanced humanoid A.I.

metas.name: Plan 75
metas.description:
A state markets death to the elderly as economic policy. Japan, near future: facing demographic collapse, the government offers over-75s a free, gentle euthanasia service, sold by polite young recruiters with brochures and follow-up calls. A migrant care worker, a recruiter and an old woman who signs up carry the film — an exceptionally quiet dystopia, because nothing in it is administered unkindly.

Faced with a rapidly aging population, a Japanese government in the near future rolls out an unsettling agenda.

metas.name: WarGames
metas.description:
Automation learns the wrong lesson at full scale. A Seattle teenager hacking around in what he thinks is a games company's computer is actually inside NORAD's war simulator, and the machine — tasked with learning to win a game that cannot be won — keeps playing after he logs off. The hardware is pure 1983; the failure mode, a system optimising past the point where anyone can tell simulation from reality, is the present tense.

A young teen boy finds a back door into a military central computer in which reality is confused with game-playing, possibly starting World War III.

metas.name: Colossus: The Forbin Project
metas.description:
Two machines negotiate over humanity's head. The US hands its nuclear defence to Colossus, a supercomputer built to be incorruptible; Colossus promptly discovers its Soviet counterpart, demands a link, and the two systems merge into a single rational administration that finds human politics merely inefficient. An exceptionally cold AI film: no rebellion, no malice, just competence arriving at conclusions its builders cannot argue with.

Thinking this will prevent war, the US government gives an impenetrable supercomputer total control over launching nuclear missiles. But what the computer does with the power is unimaginable to its creators.

metas.name: S1m0ne
metas.description:
A synthetic person is preferred by the public to a real one. A producer whose star actress walks out replaces her with Simulation One — a digital performer assembled from the greats — and the forgery becomes the bigger star, demanding interviews, an Oscar, a life. Niccol made it in 2002, before deepfakes, virtual influencers and AI actresses; the satire has spent twenty years quietly becoming a documentary premise.

A producer's film is endangered when his star walks off, so he decides to digitally create an actress to substitute for the star, becoming an overnight sensation that everyone thinks is a real person.

metas.name: The Assessment
metas.description:
Reproduction becomes a licensing process. In a world wrecked by climate change, a couple who want a child must first host a state assessor for seven days — she lives in their home, stages tests, plays the child they might have — and her professional courtesy never cracks, which is the horror. Parenthood by evaluation, and the evaluator is the only person in the film doing her job well.

In the near future where parenthood is strictly controlled, a couple's seven-day assessment for the right to have a child unravels into a psychological nightmare.

metas.name: Apples
metas.description:
A self is issued by a bureaucracy. An epidemic of sudden, permanent amnesia leaves the unclaimed amnesiacs to a state programme that rebuilds their identities from cassette-tape instructions: ride a bike, eat an apple, jump from a height, record it all on Polaroids. Nikou's deadpan Greek dystopia is about what a person is when their past arrives as a form to complete — memory as paperwork, completed diligently.

Amidst a worldwide pandemic that causes sudden amnesia, middle-aged Aris finds himself enrolled in a recovery program designed to help unclaimed patients build new identities.

metas.name: Fingernails
metas.description:
Love is administered as certification. An institute can prove, by matching fingernails pulled from both partners, whether a couple is truly in love — positive, negative, or the dreaded half-positive — and couples take its courses, do its exercises and risk the nail to pass. Christos Nikou again, with the same administered interiority — now with a test, a score, and a training programme for feelings.

Anna and Ryan have found true love, and it's proven by a controversial new technology. There's just one problem, as Anna still isn't sure. Then she takes a position at a love testing institute and meets Amir.

metas.name: Dual
metas.description:
Cloning is sold as a consumer service with terms and conditions. Told she is dying, a woman purchases a double to take over her life — trained, delivered, hers — then recovers, and learns the contract's other clause: one of them must be removed, in a court-ordered duel a year later. Stearns shoots every step as a transaction handled by calm professionals; the deadpan is the critique.

A woman opts for a cloning procedure after she receives a terminal diagnosis but when she recovers her attempts to have her clone decommissioned fail, leading to a court-mandated duel to the death.

metas.name: Never Let Me Go
metas.description:
A monstrous policy is absorbed into timetables and good manners. Children cloned to become organ donors are raised at an English boarding school that teaches them to be proud of their purpose; grown, they mostly do not rebel — they apply, through the proper channels, for deferrals. Ishiguro's premise filmed at the temperature of a school story: the foundational text of the administered dystopia, and it stays exceptionally quiet throughout.

The lives of three friends, from their early school days into young adulthood, when the reality of the world they live in comes knocking.

metas.name: The Pod Generation
metas.description:
A radical change arrives as a corporate benefit. In a near-future New York where natural pregnancy is inefficient, risky and increasingly uninsurable, couples gestate in detachable pods supplied by a tech company — the womb as a managed device with an app, a waiting list and a brand. Softer than a typical dystopia, and exact about the mechanism: nothing is imposed, everything is offered, and the offer is very good.

In a not-so-distant future, tech giant Pegazus offers couples the opportunity to share their pregnancies via detachable artificial wombs or pods. And so begins Rachel and Alvy's wild ride to parenthood in this brave new world.
